key_insight: A trust-limited Gaussian-process surrogate can accelerate NEB path searches for polaron hopping while staying anchored to DFT-verified configurations.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reproducible migration-barrier calculations for defect and ion-transport studies in complex materials where self-consistent electronic localization makes standard NEB expensive.
method: Joint energy-force Gaussian process with Matérn covariance guides elastic-band updates.
Active-atom RMS and max-displacement trust limits trigger new first-principles samples before surrogate drift.
Independent full-band DFT verification is used to confirm the final NEB path and forces.
evidence_signal: Three 96-atom DFT-verified runs with 11, 13, and 15 images produced consistent barriers of 0.1645, 0.1637, and 0.1640 eV, and a 324-atom run gave 0.1302 eV.
watch_item: Results are sensitive to supercell size and charge-transfer-region localization switching, so surrogate settings and verification steps must be carefully calibrated.
paper_title: Trust-Limited Machine-Learning-Accelerated Nudged Elastic Band Calculations for Small-Polaron Hopping in Rutile TiO2
